evidence: Cic. Att. 16.2.3 (Lewis & Short s.v. plaudō): manūs suās in plaudendō cōnsūmere
terms.comment: No ancient clapping rhyme is known; plaudō is the classical verb for clapping the hands.
Post-Augustan prose, of clapping for joy or grief (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: Omnēs gentēs, plaudite manibus; jūbilāte Deō in vōce exsultātiōnis
phrases.english: Clap your hands, all you nations; shout to God with a voice of joy

sources: Lewis & Short: plaudo · Lewis & Short: complodo
The psalm from the Latinitas loci collection (loci-vulgata).
No ancient clapping rhyme is known; the call is ours, built on the classical verb.
